newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's military to manage mass labour scheme.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's military to manage mass labour scheme.

text.p: Vietnam said on Tuesday it planned using the country's estimated 572,000-strong military to manage a proposed compulsory labour programme involving millions of young people.

In an interview with the Quan Doi Nhan Dan (People's Army) newspaper, National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh said the military's discipline and expertise in managing huge resources made it the obvious choice for running the programme.

"With their organisation and management experience it would be easy to gather people and make strength out of a labour force," Manh, who ranks fourth in Vietnam's power hierarchy, was quoted as saying.

He added that the ruling politburo planned issuing instructions to the defence ministry and communist youth organisations to establish initial teams of youth labourers for work on large infrastructure projects.
"From that we will work out a suitable management mechanism for a compulsory labour force," he said.
Vietnam has operated a compulsory labour scheme for some time under which young people are required to work on state projects for free for 10 days each year, or pay an exemption fee.
But in January this year Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet proposed an expansion of the programme, through a widening of the existing age-band and increased exemption charges.
The move drew criticism from some economists, who likened the proposal to discredited labour programmes used by communist governments during the 1950s.

Kiet, considered a leading reformist, said the new force would enable the construction of vast infrastructure projects, including a $5.5 billion 1,800 km (1,100 mile) north-south expressway running down Vietnam's mountainous spine.
